landmarks.name: Gantry Plaza State Park
landmarks.fact: Its giant gantries once loaded rail cars onto river barges.
landmarks.about: Gantry Plaza State Park is a 12-acre (4.9 ha) state park on the East River in the Hunters Point section of Long Island City, in the New York City borough of Queens. The park is located in a former dockyard and manufacturing district, and includes remnants of facilities from the area's past.
landmarks.credit: Joe Mabel from Seattle, US CC BY-SA 2.0

landmarks.name: Queensboro Plaza
landmarks.fact: An elevated station where the 7 and N/W trains meet above the streets.
landmarks.about: The Queensboro Plaza station (originally named the Queensboro Bridge Plaza station or simply Bridge Plaza station) is an elevated New York City Subway station at Queens Plaza (originally called Queensboro Bridge Plaza or simply Bridge Plaza) in the Long Island City neighborhood of Queens.

landmarks.name: Silvercup Studios
landmarks.fact: An old bread bakery turned TV studio; The Sopranos filmed here.
landmarks.about: Silvercup Studios is a film and television production facility in New York City. The studio is located in Long Island City, Queens, with another facility in the Port Morris neighborhood of the Bronx.

landmarks.name: One Court Square
landmarks.fact: Queens' tallest building for decades, a lone green glass tower.
landmarks.about: One Court Square, also known as the Citicorp Building or the Citigroup Building, is a 50-story, 673-foot (205 m) office tower in Long Island City, Queens, across the East River from Manhattan in New York City, United States.

landmarks.name: Astoria Park
landmarks.fact: Home to NYC's oldest and largest public pool, from 1936.
landmarks.about: Astoria Park is a 59.96-acre (24.26 ha) public park in the Astoria neighborhood of Queens in New York City. The park is situated on the eastern shore of the Hell Gate, a strait of the East River, between Ditmars Boulevard to the north and Hoyt Avenue to the south.

landmarks.name: Kaufman Astoria Studios
landmarks.fact: Silent films were shot here in the 1920s; Sesame Street is taped here now.
landmarks.about: The Kaufman Astoria Studios, known historically as the Paramount Studios Complex, is a film studio located in the Astoria neighborhood of Queens in New York City. The studio was constructed for Famous Players–Lasky in 1920, since it was close to Manhattan's Theater District.

landmarks.name: Queensbridge Park
landmarks.fact: Sits right under the Queensboro Bridge by the East River.
landmarks.about: Queensbridge Park, named for the nearby Queensboro Bridge, is a 20.34-acre (8.23 ha) city park along the East River in Long Island City, Queens, New York City.

landmarks.name: Steinway Street
landmarks.fact: Named for the piano family whose factory is still in Astoria.
landmarks.about: Steinway Street is a major, 2.4-mile (3.9 km), two-way street in the borough of Queens in New York City, New York, in the United States.

landmarks.name: LaGuardia Community College
landmarks.fact: Housed in a former factory for White Motor Company trucks.
landmarks.about: LaGuardia Community College is a public community college in New York City. It is in the Long Island City neighborhood of Queens in and part of the City University of New York.

landmarks.name: Hunters Point Library
landmarks.fact: A concrete library with windows carved into odd shapes.

targets.name: Bohemian Hall & Beer Garden
targets.fact: NYC's oldest beer garden, open since 1910.
targets.about: The Bohemian Citizens' Benevolent Society is a private benevolent society founded in 1892 in Astoria, Queens, to support Czech and Slovak immigrants to the area, as well as people of Czech and Slovak ancestry.
targets.riddle: Visit the oldest Astoria garden created by a benevolent society to support Czech and Slovak immigrants in Queens.

targets.name: Taverna Kyclades
targets.fact: A Greek seafood favorite on Ditmars Boulevard.
targets.riddle: Find this popular spot for oceanic cuisine tucked along Ditmars Boulevard.

targets.name: Elias Corner
targets.fact: Astoria's classic Greek fish taverna with no menu.
targets.riddle: In Astoria, visit this classic Greek fish taverna where you choose your meal without ever glancing at a menu.

targets.name: Court Square Diner
targets.fact: A 24-hour silver diner under the elevated tracks.
targets.riddle: Find this polished chrome eatery resting beneath the rumbling path of the overhead trains at any hour.

targets.name: MoMA PS1
targets.fact: A contemporary art space inside a former public school.
targets.about: MoMA PS1 is a contemporary art museum at 22-01 Jackson Avenue in the Long Island City neighborhood of Queens, in New York City, United States.
targets.riddle: Seek out the creative works displayed within the halls of a Long Island City building that once served as a school.

targets.name: Museum of the Moving Image
targets.fact: Home to a huge collection of movie and TV props and cameras.
targets.about: The Museum of the Moving Image (MoMI) is a time-based media museum located in a former building of the historic Astoria Studios (now Kaufman Astoria Studios), in the Astoria neighborhood of Queens in New York City.
targets.riddle: Explore a former Astoria Studios building where historic cameras and iconic cinema props are now kept for public view.

targets.name: Noguchi Museum
targets.fact: Sculptor Isamu Noguchi designed it himself around a garden.
targets.about: The Noguchi Museum (chartered as The Isamu Noguchi Foundation and Garden Museum) is a museum and sculpture garden at 32-37 Vernon Boulevard in the Long Island City neighborhood of Queens in New York City.
targets.riddle: Stroll through a tranquil garden retreat designed by a master sculptor in the heart of Long Island City.

targets.name: SculptureCenter
targets.fact: A contemporary sculpture space in a former trolley repair shop.
targets.about: SculptureCenter is a not-for-profit, contemporary art museum located in Long Island City, Queens, New York City. It was founded in 1928 as "The Clay Club" by Dorothea Denslow.
targets.riddle: Once a place to fix trolleys, this Long Island City space now displays modern works founded as The Clay Club.

targets.name: Socrates Sculpture Park
targets.fact: Artists turned an illegal dump into an outdoor sculpture park.
targets.about: Socrates Sculpture Park is an outdoor museum and public park where artists can create and exhibit sculptures and multi-media installations. It is located one block from the Noguchi Museum at the intersection of Broadway and Vernon Boulevard in the neighborhood of Astoria, Queens, New York City.
targets.riddle: Once an illegal dump, this Astoria space now showcases art at the intersection of Broadway and Vernon Boulevard.

targets.name: Rainey Park
targets.fact: A small riverside park named for a local who pushed for the Queensboro Bridge.
targets.riddle: Stroll by the river where a dedicated local advocated for the nearby bridge to connect our borough.

targets.name: Hunters Point South Park
targets.fact: A waterfront park with a view of the Manhattan skyline and the UN.
targets.riddle: Stare across the water at the city horizon and the world assembly from this scenic riverside green.

targets.name: Athens Square
targets.fact: A plaza with Greek columns and statues of Socrates and Athena.
targets.riddle: Visit this plaza to admire towering stone pillars alongside statues of a famous philosopher and a goddess of wisdom.

targets.name: Pepsi-Cola Sign
targets.fact: A landmark neon sign from 1936, moved to Gantry Plaza.
targets.about: The Pepsi-Cola sign is a neon sign at Gantry Plaza State Park in the Long Island City neighborhood of Queens in New York City. The sign, visible from Manhattan and the East River, was built in 1940 and originally installed atop PepsiCo (previously Pepsi-Cola)'s bottling factory nearby.
targets.riddle: Visible from Manhattan, this glowing relic once sat atop a bottling factory and now shines at Gantry Plaza State Park.

targets.name: Hell Gate Bridge
targets.fact: It was the world's longest steel arch bridge when it opened in 1917.
targets.about: The Hell Gate Bridge (originally the New York Connecting Railroad Bridge) is a railroad bridge in New York City. The bridge carries two tracks of Amtrak's Northeast Corridor and one freight track between Astoria, Queens, and Port Morris, Bronx, via Randalls and Wards Islands.
targets.riddle: I am a massive steel arch carrying trains between Astoria and the Bronx over the islands.

targets.name: Queensboro Bridge
targets.fact: Simon & Garfunkel called it the 59th Street Bridge.
targets.about: The Queensboro, officially the Ed Koch Queensboro Bridge, but known by locals by one of two other names depending on the side, is a cantilever bridge over the East River in New York City.
targets.riddle: Simon and Garfunkel sang of this cantilever path spanning the East River, which locals know by two different names.
